representation: A population bar for 1,000 people, a positive-test bar split into true-positive and false-positive shares, and a posterior bar with a 50% reference marker.
motion: prevalence changes the diseased and false-positive widths
sensitivity changes the true-positive share and posterior
the 50% marker pulses as a fixed reference
checkpoints: read the posterior rather than sensitivity
misconceptionTest: At low prevalence the posterior stays far below 50% and below sensitivity, even at 90% sensitivity, because many false positives enter the positive-test bar. This tests both 'positive means very likely' and 'base rate does not matter'.
accessibility: Rows are named with text, TP and FP are identified by position and text, the 50% marker is labeled, sliders are keyboard accessible, and alt text summarizes the count relationship.
